title: Dhaba-Style Palak Paneer
tagline: Silky blanched-spinach gravy with golden paneer cubes, finished with cream and kasuri methi.

substitutes.name: Boiled potato
substitutes.note: Cube 2 boiled potatoes and pan-fry until crisp.

substitutes.name: Curd
substitutes.note: Whisk 2 tbsp curd with ½ tsp besan so it doesn't split; add off the heat.

substitutes.name: Cashews
substitutes.note: Soak 8 cashews in hot water for 10 min and blend to a paste.

substitutes.name: Milk
substitutes.note: 3 tbsp full-fat milk, simmered for 2 extra minutes.

substitutes.name: Garam masala
substitutes.note: Use ¼ tsp; different aroma but still warm and savoury.

steps.text: Boil water in a pot, add the spinach and blanch for 2 minutes. Drain and plunge into cold water to keep it bright green.
steps.tip: The ice-water dip is what keeps the colour vivid.

steps.text: Grind the blanched spinach with the green chilli into a smooth puree.
Heat half the oil and pan-fry the paneer cubes until lightly golden, about 3 minutes. Set aside.
In the same kadai, heat the remaining oil. Sauté the onion until golden, about 5 minutes, then add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree and salt and cook until the oil separates, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the spinach puree and a splash of water. Simmer for 3 minutes.
steps.tip: Don't simmer longer or the spinach turns olive-dull.

steps.text: Add the paneer, garam masala and kasuri methi. Turn off the heat and swirl in the cream.
Serve with hot rotis, naan or jeera rice.

missing_summary: Add fresh cream and kasuri methi and you can make Dhaba-Style Palak Paneer.
tips: No cream? Curd works if you add it off the heat.
Leftovers make a great sandwich filling the next morning.
